Four MT Forest Wildfire Vehicles for Upper Austria
27.08.2026

The summer of 2026 was exceptionally dry across large parts of Europe, bringing an increased risk of wildfire even to regions that have traditionally been unaffected. However, the trend of recent decades is clear: longer periods without rainfall are increasingly alternating with extreme precipitation events. The result will be more wildfire and natural disaster incidents in the future. To effectively respond to both, fire services require highly capable off-road vehicles. For this reason, the Upper Austrian Fire Service Association (Landes-Feuerwehrverband Oberösterreich) has recently procured four MT Forest vehicles. 

 

A Strategic Support Network in Upper Austria 

Upper Austria is located in northern Austria, bordering both Germany and the Czech Republic, while stretching southward into the Alps. Its topography ranges from the lowlands along the Danube River to alpine peaks, and its vegetation spans extensive agricultural areas as well as densely forested regions. The Upper Austrian Fire Service Association comprises 905 fire departments with approximately 95,000 members.  

According to Deputy Provincial Fire Commander Michael Hutterer, the association prepares its members for wildfire response through targeted training programs. In addition, a support-unit structure introduced decades ago ensures rapid aerial assistance via helicopters during wildfire incidents. 

“Over the past few years, we have also procured specialized vehicles such as pickups equipped for vegetation firefighting. Further acquisitions, including ATVs (All-Terrain Vehicles), are already being planned,” says Hutterer. 

 

Off-Road Vehicles: A Key Factor in Wildfire Response 

Hutterer clearly outlines the challenge: “The rapidly changing climate and the fact that disaster deployments will soon become routine rather than exceptional is evident from the growing number of forest and vegetation fires across Austria and Europe.” 

This development not only poses a threat to people and ecosystems but also pushes fire services and their existing equipment to their operational limits. Hutterer explains why off-road vehicles will become increasingly important in the future: “Wildfire suppression is extremely labor-intensive and physically demanding for emergency personnel. The right vehicles can reach much closer to the incident scene, eliminating the need to carry equipment over long distances on foot. This significantly increases operational effectiveness while at the same time greatly reducing the burden on crews.” 

This is precisely why four Rosenbauer MT Forest vehicles were recently commissioned as TLF 3000 VBB units, a designation standing for water tender with a specialization in vegetation fire suppression. One vehicle has been stationed in each of Upper Austria’s four administrative regions, ensuring that assistance is never far away when needed. 

 

The Advantages of the MT Forest: More Than Wildfire Response 

The procurement of the new vehicles was primarily driven by their outstanding off-road capability. Yet these capabilities are valuable not only during wildfires but also when infrastructure has been damaged, for example by landslides or debris flows. In such cases, a water tender can transport service water to otherwise inaccessible areas. Thanks to its polypropylene (PP) tank, the MT Forest is ideally suited for this task. 

“Versatility was a major advantage for us,” explains Hutterer. “In addition, we placed great importance on ensuring that these vehicles can be operational and effective very quickly.” 

 

The Chassis: A Critical Component 

The MT Forest can be built on various chassis platforms. The Upper Austrian Fire Service Association selected a Tatra chassis, whose Force series offers a unique concept proven across a wide range of demanding applications. 

Its central backbone tube frame combined with independently suspended swinging half-axles ensures exceptional ground contact regardless of terrain conditions. At the same time, the driveshaft and axle shafts are protected within tubular structures. The air lines for the Central Tire Inflation System (CTIS) are also routed through these tubes, protecting them from damage. Particularly important for firefighting operations, brake lines and cable harnesses are equipped with heat protection throughout the chassis. 

Another key advantage is the vehicle’s overall height of only 3.10 meters while still providing a fording depth of 1.20 meters and the ability to handle gradients of up to 68 percent. Thanks to its air suspension system, the vehicle body can be lowered by 80 mm or raised by 120 mm as required. A further highlight is that the Roll Over Protection System (ROPS) is already integrated into the cab, eliminating the need for aftermarket installation. 

 

An Unusual Approach: The Chassis Supplier Orders the Bodywork 

The procurement of the vehicles was handled by Tschann, the exclusive sales and service partner for Tatra commercial vehicles in Austria, South Tyrol, and Bavaria. As part of the package, Tschann also provides a full day of driver and chassis training, including off-road instruction. 

In a departure from the usual procurement process, Tschann, as the chassis supplier, commissioned Rosenbauer to build the firefighting bodywork. 

Looking at the vehicle itself, one of the first noticeable features is the branch deflector mounted above the cab. At the front, the RM15C electronically controlled monitor is equipped with a dedicated wildfire nozzle that reduces water consumption. In addition, firefighters can attack fires through a roof hatch using a handheld nozzle. 

Both the monitor and the nozzle are supplied by an N35 fire pump, which can operate even while the vehicle is moving. Water is carried in a 3,400-liter PP tank, while a separate foam tank holds 100 liters of foam concentrate. The integrated Variomatic 48 system provides precise proportioning for wetting agents and firefighting foam production. 

 

A Convincing Result 

The chassis and firefighting bodywork form an excellent combination, both technically and in terms of project execution, as Michael Hutterer summarizes: 

“The planning and implementation process was characterized by constructive collaboration and open dialogue between equal partners, with Rosenbauer as our long-standing and reliable partner and Tschann as an experienced specialist in the firefighting sector.” 

The result is, in his words, “a highly convincing vehicle” whose “robust technology, ease of operation, and truly exceptional off-road performance” make it stand out. 

“The fact that these MT Forest vehicles can access areas that would be impossible for most firefighting vehicles represents an enormous advantage for us. The future will show that they will be valuable not only in wildfire operations, but also when infrastructure has been destroyed, roads have been washed away, or transportation routes have been blocked by landslides and debris flows.”
